summary.headline: Steel Strips Wheels Q2 FY27 revenue rose 61% YoY to INR1,930 crore and standalone EBITDA per wheel hit INR404, with management reiterating the figure as sustainable.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the strongest quarter in company history, with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT. Standalone EBITDA including other income rose 107% YoY to INR237 crore, margin 12.3% vs 9.6%, and PAT rose 209% to INR119 crore. Management attributed the gains to richer aluminium mix, cost optimisation, higher exports and customer price revisions for non-raw-material input costs. A supplementary invoicing of INR140 crore in Q2 (INR183 crore in H1) relating to raw-material pass-through was disputed by analysts as flattering EBITDA; management said it has no bearing on EBITDA. The board also approved a greenfield plant at Sambhajinagar (INR1,400 crore over 60 months) and an interim dividend of INR1.50 per share.

financial_highlights.change: Management says not an EBITDA item

segments.name: Alloy (aluminium) wheels
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q2 revenue and 42% of H1 revenue; volume about 12 lakh units in Q2 and 23 lakh in H1. Aluminium wheel capacity running near full, with debottlenecking taking output to about 5.4 million annualised (10% uplift).

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Highest growth among segments in Q2 across domestic and export markets; domestic steel wheel demand up 28% in H1 per management. Management expects record CV sales in October.

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: Market share rose to 45% from 43%; tractor volume up about 15% in H1 per management.

segments.name: Aluminium knuckles
segments.commentary: Progressing in line with expectations; seeking more customer approvals. Commercial production expected in Q4 FY27 at Bhuj with 1.1 million units annual capacity.

segments.name: Steel wheels / high vent hole
segments.commentary: Rising demand for high vent hole steel wheels that resemble aluminium; management says EBITDA per wheel for aluminium (incl. knuckles) is about 40% above steel overall, and about 2x for pure passenger car.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance at start of year: top-line growth above 20% and EBITDA per wheel above INR310; H1 has exceeded both, and management is 'extremely confident' of strong guidance for the remaining two quarters.
EBITDA per wheel of INR404 described as sustainable and possibly exceeded if October trend continues; management did not give a quantified FY28 number.
FY27 export target of INR600 crore on track; management said it could reach INR700-750 crore depending on a US trade deal.
Target export of at least INR1,500 crore (possibly INR2,000 crore) in about 3 years.
Management said capex for FY27 is over INR600 crore (Bhuj INR420 crore, Dappar tractor wheels INR120 crore, machinery replacement and automation about INR70 crore).
capex_capacity: Bhuj aluminium wheel plant adds 1.2 million wheels annually, taking aluminium capacity beyond 6.2 million; commercial start early April 2027.
Bhuj aluminium knuckle facility with 1.1 million units annual capacity; commercial production targeted in Q4 FY27.

Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) greenfield: INR1,400 crore over 60 months, funded by debt, internal accruals and likely strategic partners; subject to regulatory clearances. Adds 1.6 million steel wheels (1.0 million passenger car, 0.6 million OTR) and 2.5 million aluminium wheels, plus hot stamping line (1.3 million strokes p.a., about INR400 crore turnover, around INR170 crore investment, anchor customer in Maharashtra).
Hot stamping production targeted for Q1 calendar 2027 commissioning, with commercial start around the same time or later; management says plant will start sold out.

Dappar tractor wheel capacity addition of about 0.5 million tractor sets (INR120 crore). Post-expansion aluminium capacity: about 9.1 million with Sambhajinagar; management expects 80%+ utilisation in new facilities in FY28 and 100% within 3-4 months of commissioning.
demand_pricing: Management attributed price increases to customer revisions for non-raw-material input costs; said OEMs accepted price increases to fund new capacity.
Pricing in steel wheels previously described as 'abysmally low'; management says it has stopped working on those margins.
Management said CV customers are seeking product, and October CV sales expected to be the highest ever; tractor volumes up about 15% in H1.

Export competition: main competitor for aluminium wheels is Turkey; China faces anti-dumping duties in the US, so Indian suppliers do not currently sell to the US. Qualification cycle with OEMs is about 9 months.
Hot stamping competitors named: Gestamp, JBM, Autogen (Korea).

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable EBITDA per wheel, and what is the H1 figure excluding the INR183 crore pass-on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the supplementary invoicing is a raw-material pass-through with no EBITDA impact; INR404 per wheel in Q2 is sustainable and could improve if October trend holds.

qa_highlights.question: What IRR/ROCE is expected on the INR1,400 crore Sambhajinagar project and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE should exceed the current 24% (H1 FY27) and declined to give project IRR; funding is a mix of debt, internal accruals and strategic partners (commodity players that have been partners since the factory started).

qa_highlights.question: Analyst estimate implies only 12-13% incremental ROCE at INR400 per wheel for Sambhajinagar; how does management respond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share its numbers, citing operational efficiency, proximity to customers, freight savings and automation, and said the plant will be at least 25% more productive than current operations.

qa_highlights.question: Is aluminium EBITDA per wheel twice steel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 40% gap refers to the overall mix including CV, tractor and EV; for pure passenger car aluminium vs steel it is about twice.

qa_highlights.question: Will exports reach INR1,500 crore in 3 years and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,500 crore is visible in 3 years, driven by OEM steel wheel approvals in Europe (MAN, Scania, Daimler), with certifications taking 12 years to obtain; export ramp expected from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks if CV and tractor volumes taper off from a high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged a volume decline would affect EBITDA per wheel but said customers are seeking product and October CV sales would be a record; tractor growth expected at 10-15%.

risks_watch: Analysts questioned whether the INR140 crore Q2 (INR183 crore H1) supplementary invoicing inflates EBITDA per wheel; management disputed this. Watch whether reported per-wheel margins hold in Q3-Q4.
Sustainability of INR404 EBITDA per wheel after price pass-through benefits and high CV/tractor volume base.
Execution risk on Bhuj (aluminium wheels April 2027, knuckles Q4 FY27) and Sambhajinagar (hot stamping Q1 CY2027).
Debt funding of INR1,400 crore Sambhajinagar project; analysts flagged already high debt. Strategic partner not named.
US trade deal and freight costs (Hormuz / Iran war mentioned) affecting export volumes and competitiveness.
Management did not disclose project IRR; analyst estimates of 12-13% incremental ROCE were disputed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on growth and margins, but defensive when questioned on the supplementary invoicing and on the EBITDA per wheel premise; declined to give project IRR, customer names or segment-level numbers.
key_quotes: So the second quarter of financial year '27 was the strongest quarter in the company's history with the highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
This INR183 crores supplementary invoicing is only based on raw material price changes, which are a pass-through.
SSWL is the lowest cost producer of aluminum wheels and steel wheels in the world, barring China.
So we told the OEMs, if you want me to build a factory, we have to pay for it.
